title: Consult chair affect, uptake and teach-back

definition.object: a doctor-patient consultation (clinic or teleconsult) read as a whole; the affect of the PATIENT in the chair
definition.unscorable: no speaker or no transcript characters: unscorable, never neutral
principles: trajectory (open to close) matters more than one moment
report rates and means across consults, never the modal bucket alone on a three-level scale

distress.low: composed help-seeking; concern is named but turn-taking holds and no functional break or fear language drives the visit
distress.medium: pain or fear is doing work in the chair (a functional limit, a named fear, a second opinion after sudden news) while the patient can still give a history
distress.high: breaks the consultation: crying, unable to answer, the talk cannot proceed; rare, do not inflate medium

confusion.low: follows the plan; at most one clarification
confusion.medium: needs repeats, hits a language or plan barrier, talks past the question, or still wants an in-person explanation after the plan landed
confusion.high: never takes in what was asked across the whole consultation

frustration.low: none, or only connection checks at the start
frustration.medium: repeated repair loops (language, screen, connection, device) that eat the consultation: PROCESS frustration
frustration.high: anger at the doctor or at the process; do not inflate process repair loops to high
frustration.note: process frustration and clinical frustration (anger at earlier care) are different things and must not stand in for each other

reassurance.low: plan given but the patient stays guarded, still asks for more detail or an in-person visit, or the close does not answer a named concern
reassurance.medium: thanks or agreement with residual caution; plan accepted; no named fear was the opening load, or a mild concern closed without a clear calmer shift
reassurance.high: the close is clearly calmer than the opening, or a named fear got an explicit answer

anti_defaults: medium reassurance is not the dump bin: a patient saying okay or thanks is not enough
if the opening had a named fear and the close answered it, reassurance is high
if the close is still guarded after the plan, reassurance is low

uptake.known_gap: no logistics code: a site too far is a refusal of the site, not of the care

aggregation.flat_default: distress low AND confusion low AND frustration low AND reassurance medium; a high rate can be a true pattern of short calm consultations, not a scoring bug

cases_overlay.citation: Laws et al., Patient Education and Counseling 2013;91:192-199 (CASES)
cases_overlay.rule: the structural overlay never replaces or merges into the four affect axes; engagement as a process is not reassurance

layers.A: light structural tags per consultation: dominant mix (presentation heavy, resolution present, engagement present, mixed, process friction, unscorable), engagement process (present, absent, lecture only), information present, doctor effect proxy (fear assuaged, load eased, load held, flat no load, process friction, unknown)
layers.B: per recommendation as a mini-thread: owner (patient, doctor, unclear), induction (problem presentation, request, focused question, invitation, cued, unclear), resolution type (patient agrees, patient refuses, neither, deferred, provider action, information only, not resolved, empathy only)
layers.C: threads with owner, induction, processes present and resolution types, plus non-thread talk (socialising, agenda setting, wrap-up, physical exam, connection repair); utterance shares stay null unless estimable

definition.engine_note: engine llm_zdr since v1.0.0. The Jev typed questions above mirror the booleans and code-like items; Jev is not used until its own bench passes (draft status, S7-1).
definition.bench_population: Meet teleconsultations of one clinician plus a 28-consult cut, single rater; no room tape. CASES heuristic sidecars are not human gold.

questions.text: How distressed is the patient in the chair, by the distress anchors (disease severity is not distress)?
How far does the patient fail to follow the plan, by the confusion anchors?
How much frustration is there (process repair loops versus anger at the doctor or the process), by the frustration anchors?
How reassured is the patient at the close compared with the opening, by the reassurance anchors and anti-defaults?
Does the patient restate the plan in their own words: none, partial or full?
Is there an engagement process (the doctor invites and answers the patient's own concerns), only a lecture, or none?
Does the doctor give information or a plan in the consultation?
For one audible recommendation, how does the patient respond?
For one recommendation, how does its thread resolve?
